The New York Yankees are turning to Cy Young Award hopeful Cam Schlittler to start the first game of the 2026 postseason.

Schlittler has been tabbed to start Game 1 of the Yankees' Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox, per ESPN's Jorge Castillo .

The Yankees will then turn to Max Fried for Game 2 and Gerrit Cole for Game 3 if necessary, per Castillo.

Yankees vs. Red Sox AL Wild Card Preview 🔮

The Yankees are set to begin their upcoming series against the Red Sox Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.

The series will resume Wednesday and, if necessary, continue Thursday.

Should the Yankees advance to the ALDS, the club is scheduled to begin the series with away games the following Saturday and Monday.

Right-handed Schlittler last pitched three innings Sept. 24 against the Tampa Bay Rays. He finished the season with a 1.95 ERA, the lowest from any Yankees pitcher since 1978.

Fried, a southpaw, last pitched 6.2 innings Sept. 22, also against the Rays, on his way to a 2.80 season-long ERA.

Yankees pitching coach Matt Blake said last Thursday Fried was "obviously in heavy consideration" to start Game 1, in part to give Schlittler more time between outings, per Hoch .

"Max is on extended rest, and Cam would be on his third five day in a row," Blake said Thursday, per Hoch. "So just making sure he's in a good spot before we make any rash decisions."

Fried has held Red Sox batters to a .146 batting average and .473 OPS in two starts this season, while the rival club batted .174 with a .560 OPS against Schlittler.

The Yankees dropped Game 1 of the ALDS to the Red Sox last fall with Fried starting, then came back to win the series behind starts from Carlos Rodón and Schlittler.

Last season marked just the third time since the Wild Card round was introduced in 2020 a club recovered from losing Game 1 to advance to the divisional series. The Yankees will now hope Schlittler can help his club avoid the need for another comeback next week.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million contract changed baseball forever: Here’s where the Los Angeles Dodgers star’s record deal really goes and what it means for MLB's future
articles.summary: Explore how Shohei Ohtani's unprecedented $700 million contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers is reshaping MLB's financial landscape, attracting global attention, and influencing player compensation models.
articles.body: Shohei Ohtani’s signing with the Los Angeles Dodgers in December 2023 has produced one of the strangest financial arrangements in MLB history. The headline figure was a staggering 10 years and $700 million. But the structure behind that number was just as important, with much of the money deferred into the future, rather than paid out during his playing contract.The agreement was more than just a salary story. Ohtani arrived in Los Angeles as one of baseball’s most recognisable stars, with a built-in international following and immense commercial value. His Dodgers jersey broke Fanatics’ 48-hour sales record, and his presence helped solidify the franchise’s connections to Japanese fans and businesses.Shohei Ohtani’s Dodgers contract creates a remarkable financial story beyond the $700 million headlineThe first big one. Ohtani is not going to get 70 million dollars a year for the 10-year playing term. The deal will pay him $2 million annually from 2024 through 2033, totalling $20 million over the 10 seasons. The remaining $680 million is deferred and paid at the rate of $68 million per year from 2034 through 2043.That structure significantly alters how the contract impacts the Dodgers' Competitive Balance Tax calculations. For CBT purposes, deferred compensation is valued at its present-day worth, MLB said. Since so much of Ohtani’s money is being paid out more than a decade from now, the present value of the contract was calculated at roughly $460 million, which yielded a yearly CBT figure of roughly $46 million, as opposed to the headline annual value of $70 million.Contract detailShohei Ohtani’s dealTotal contract value$700 millionContract length10 yearsPaid during playing contract$20 millionDeferred compensation$680 millionDeferred payment period2034–2043Approx. CBT value$460 millionApprox. annual CBT figure$46 millionShohei Ohtani’s Dodgers contract reshaped MLB financesThe deal gave the Los Angeles Dodgers more payroll flexibility in the short run. MLB said the idea of deferring the money came from Ohtani himself, with the player intent on helping create space for the club to build around him. MLB's collective bargaining rules allow for such deals, as they do not set a limit on the amount or percentage of compensation that can be deferred.It’s more than one player. Before Ohtani, other large contracts in MLB had included deferred compensation, but never on this magnitude. His deal showed how a superstar contract could be constructed to satisfy both immediate roster building and long-term financial commitments.Shohei Ohtani boosted Los Angeles Dodgers’ commercial reachThe Dodgers can’t quantify Ohtani’s financial impact simply by looking at how the contract will affect the payroll. There was an instant commercial reaction to the signing because of his global popularity. Ohtani’s No. 17 Los Angeles Dodgers jersey broke all-time sales records in the first 48 hours after its release, Fanatics said. It sold at more than twice the pace of the former record holder, Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami jersey.The Japanese market was a special highlight. Fanatics said Ohtani Dodgers jerseys sold in Japan for the first 48 hours were more than the number of MLB team jerseys sold in Japan in the previous two years combined. It was an early sign of the magnitude of Ohtani’s commercial appeal even before he had stepped onto the pitch for his first regular-season game for the Los Angeles Angels.His popularity carried over into his first season with the Dodgers. MLB said in July 2024 that Ohtani was No. 1 in player jersey sales in the U.S., Japan and globally. He is the first Japanese-born player to top MLB's jersey rankings since the data was first released by MLB and the MLB Players Association in 2010.That commercial pull is still there. Ohtani led the league in jersey sales for a third consecutive season in March 2026, according to MLB, which said he was the top-selling player jersey in the U.S., Japan and worldwide. Ohtani’s teammate Yoshinobu Yamamoto finished second. It was the first time that the top two players entering an MLB season were Japanese-born.A burgeoning link to Japan has also helped the larger Dodgers brand. Ohtani was joined by another big Japanese star in Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and the organization boosted its commercial presence by partnering with Japanese companies. Those developments help explain why Ohtani’s contract became as much a business story as a baseball one.Los Angeles Dodgers turned Ohtani investment into growthThe most dramatic assertion about Ohtani’s financial impact came in October 2025. MLB insider Joon Lee reported that sources felt the Dodgers had essentially earned the entire $700 million worth of Ohtani’s contract in his first season with ticket sales, merchandise and marketing deals in Japan and other international markets.This should be regarded as a reported estimate, not as audited proof that every dollar of the contract was literally recovered. There are also broader team operations in the underlying income streams, and they may not be solely attributable to Ohtani. But the report reveals the extraordinary commercial hopes that accompany his arrival in Los Angeles.So the Dodgers received both sporting and commercial dividends from the investment almost immediately. Ohtani’s on-field production was eye-catching during the regular season and postseason, and his international profile kept creating opportunities outside the ballpark.That was topped by Juan Soto’s 15-year, $765 million deal with the New York Mets, the largest free-agent contract in MLB history when it was signed in December of 2024. Soto’s deal is not reliant on the same massive level of deferred compensation as Ohtani’s.That difference is significant in assessing Ohtani’s place in MLB history. His contract is no longer the biggest in the league in terms of headline value, but the structure is still very odd. A $700 million commitment, $680 million in deferrals, a roughly $46 million annual CBT figure and Ohtani’s enormous commercial footprint combined to create a model that changed the conversation around how baseball’s biggest stars can be compensated.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Colorado Rockies at Chicago White Sox game discussion: Kyle Freeland vs Anthony Kay
articles.summary: The Rockies play their final game of the season looking to end things on a high note.
articles.body:
The sun has finally risen on the last day of the last day of the 2026 Major League Baseball regular season. Today marks Game 162 of 162 an the Colorado Rockies are in the South Side of Chicago for one last game against the White Sox .

The Rockies played spoiler last night, handing a loss to the White Sox while also handing the American League Central to the Cleveland Guardians . Now the Rockies seek to end a rough September, a long campaign, and their fourth consecutive season with 100 or more losses on a high note with a win this afternoon. Should the Rockies emerge victorious, it will be their first series win since the beginning of the month.

On the mound today for the Rockies—and perhaps making his final start for his hometown team—is left-handed pitcher Kyle Freeland . It has been a long and difficult season for the 33-year-old from Denver as he has dealt with injuries and poor performances. His 6.58 ERA in 25 starts is the second worst figure of his career—trailing only a miserable 2019 where he struggled with mechanical issues and spent time in Triple-A Albuquerque.

Freeland gave up five earned runs on nine hits his last time out against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Coors Field. Should this indeed be the last time we see him suit up for the Rockies, it would be nice to see him end things with a good outing.

Toeing the rubber for the White Sox this afternoon is left-handed veteran Anthony Kay . Kay, 31, is bringing his first full MLB season since 2023 to a close. He spent the 2024 and 2025 campaigns with Japan's Yokohama DeNA Baystars.

Kay owns a 4.53 ERA in 32 appearances—30 of which were starts—for the White Sox this season. In 153 innings he has 125 strikeouts to 54 walks, though there is some wildness in him. Kay currently leads the league in hit batters with 25. His primary pitch is a sweeper that he backs up with a mid-90s four-seam fastball and a sinker. He also throws a cutter, a changeup, and a traditional slider. This will be Kay's first time facing the Rockies in his big league career.

articles.title: MLB Live Results, Scores, Highlights, Stat Milestones and Final Playoff Bracket After Game 162
articles.summary: Sunday was the final day of the 2026 Major League Baseball season, and there was plenty at stake.
articles.body:
Sunday was the final day of the 2026 Major League Baseball season, and there was plenty at stake.

There was a tie atop the AL West that got resolved when the Texas Rangers lost, handing the division title to the Houston Astros. When the Philadelphia Phillies won their game, they finally buried the Arizona Diamondbacks in the NL Wild Card race. There were also a handful of individual stat races that went down to the wire.

Scroll down for all updates as we covered everything that happened for Game 162.

And a fine speech by Joe Espada, too. It's possible he won't be back in 2027, but he's clearly keen on making this one count.

The Giants' former pitcher and beloved color commentator has called it a career (broadcasting, that is) after 36 years at the mic. Today was a day to honor him, and to officially rename the booth he has shared with Duane Kuiper the "Kruk and Kuip Broadcast Booth."

The Astros Celebrate Winning the AL West

True, their 81-81 record is the worst ever for a division winner in baseball history. Yet a division title is never not worth celebrating, especially when the fight for it goes all the way to Game 162.

The Angels last made the playoffs in 2014, making for the longest drought of any team in MLB. But hey, at least they didn't sink as low as 100 losses between 2015 and 2025.

The Phillies Pop Bottles in the Clubhouse

It went down to the wire, but a fifth straight postseason appearance is always worth celebrating. The season certainly turned when Don Mattingly took over, with the Phillies securing 79 of their 88 wins under his watch.

It's the 12th 100-win season in their history, and their sixth in the last decade.

Sandy Alcantara Opens and Closes the Marlins' Season

Sandy Alcantara becoming the Marlins' closer in addition to their ace was on nobody's 2026 bingo card, but it's pretty cool.

He ends the year with 13 wins and three saves. The last guy to do that while also making 30 starts in a season was Phil Niekro in 1973.

Pete Crow-Armstrong and Kyle Schwarber both went homerless on Sunday, resulting in a first-place tie with 45 apiece atop the MLB leaderboard.

They're the first co-home run champs since Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Salvador Perez in 2021, and the first in the NL since Nolan Arenado and Chris Carter in 2016.

A 4-1 win over the Tigers nudged the Pirates' 2026 record to 82-80, giving them their first winning record since 2018. This calls for the jolly roger.

There you go. Feast your eyes. The action starts on Tuesday in Atlanta, where the Phillies will take on the Braves in Game 1 of a best-of-three set.

Astros Secure AL West Title with Rangers Loss

That's it for the AL West race. The Rangers needed to beat the Twins and for the A's to beat the Astros. Despite a late Corey Seager home run, the Rangers could not do the latter in losing 6-4 to the Twins.

Houston secures the AL's No. 3 seed and will host the Chicago White Sox in the AL Wild Card Series.

The NL playoff field is set, and the AL bracket isn't far off from being complete in its own right.

The Astros have a 8-0 lead on the A's in the seventh, and just need to hold on. The Rangers trail the Twins 6-2 in the eighth, and need both a dramatic rally and an Astros collapse.

Phillies Clinch Final NL Wild Card, Beat Rays 7-3

Winning today was the easiest way for the Phillies to get into the playoffs, and they have done it. The NL's third Wild Card is theirs, and they will face the Atlanta Braves in the Wild Card Series.

The Diamondbacks will go home, no matter how their game against the Padres concludes.

Max Scherzer Finally Hands Over the Ball

That does it for his season, and maybe for his careeer. He finishes the day with seven innings and, as of now, one run allowed.

If he wants to get the three strikeouts he still needs to tie Justin Verlander for eighth all-time, he'll need to come back for his age-42 season.

The Diamondbacks Show Fight, Tie Padres 4-4

The Padres led this one 4-1 until Arizona put up a three spot in the top of the seventh. They're doing their job, but still need the Rays to erase a 7-3 deficit to the Phillies. That game is in the bottom of the eighth.

Max Scherzer Tells His Manager to Take a Hike

This would feel like a scripted bit, if only this wasn't a 42-year-old pitcher with 104 pitches on his arm already.

Scherzer didn't get any strikeouts in the seventh, so he's still three short of Justin Verlander and eighth on the all-time list. But go ahead, you try and tell him he's done.

He's at 97 pitches through six innings, but his seven strikeouts put him just three behind Justin Verlander for eighth on the all-time list. He's coming back out for the top of the seventh.

J.P. Crawford Gets His Moment in Seattle

This is going to be Rick Rizzs' last game in the booth. It could also be J.P. Crawford's final game for the Mariners at shortstop. His contract is up and his position could pass to Colt Emerson.

This is his 974th game as a Mariner, 10th on their all-time list.

Christian Walker Inches Astros Closer to AL West Title, Lead A's 5-0

That's Walker's 29th home run of the year, and it happened shortly after the Rangers dug themselves a 5-1 hole to the Twins.

Pat Murphy lifted "The Miz" with a runner on first and one out in the top of the sixth. That runner didn't score, so Misiorowski officially ends his season with a 1.80 ERA.

With that, he easily clears Cam Schlittler's 1.95 ERA for the MLB lead.

Diamondbacks on the Board, Still Trail Padres 3-1

Ketel Marte hit an RBI single in the top of the sixth inning, cutting Arizona's deficit to 3-1.

They'll need to keep coming back… and for the Rays to do the same in Philadelphia, where it's 7-2 Phillies in the seventh inning.

Jakob Junis walked three batters in the fifth inning, including one to bring home a run for Minnesota. Skip Schumaker lifted him for Jordan Montgomery, who is coming into a bases-loaded, one-out situation.

With the Astros still leading the A's 4-0, it might be about time to stick a fork in the Rangers.

Even Slow-Motion Jacob Misiorowski Looks Unhittable

So, that's what 100 mph looks like in super slo-mo.

Edmundo Sosa Piles On, Phillies Lead Rays 7-1

This is after he had doubled earlier in the game, so the Phillies' whole lineup is getting in on what is a 10-hit barrage so far. This is also their second home run of the inning, after that had gone six games and 189 batters in a row without even one .

With Zack Wheeler shoving on the mound, the Phillies have pretty strong clinch energy right now.

He's also almost certainly sown up the major league ERA title, with four scoreless innings dropping his ERA for the season down to 1.82.

Fun fact: "The Miz" is the third pitcher this century with over 250 strikeouts and an ERA under 2.00 in a season, joining Jacob deGrom and Pedro Martinez.

Bryce Harper Is Off the HR Schneid, Phillies Lead Rays 5-1

Harper had last homered on September 12, and this is just his second long ball since August 26.

This happened right around when Gavin Sheets put the Diamondbacks in a 2-0 hole with a solo homer in San Diego. It's looking good for the Phillies.

George Springer Exits to a Standing Ovation in Toronto

George Springer is in the last year of his contract with the Blue Jays, and he is undecided about whether he wants to return for another major league season. He turned 37 on September 19.

If this is it, happy trails to a four-time All-Star and one of the great playoff hitters baseball has ever known.

Yankees-Orioles Game 162 Is Canceled Due to Weather

The game had no stakes, so it will not be rescheduled. The Yankees and Orioles will both finish their seasons with 161 games.

One wonders how the Red Sox feel about this. They're about to face the Yankees in the Wild Card Series, and weather concerns forced a double-header on Friday and a move to Tropicana Field for what has also proven to be a stakes-free finale against the Cubs.

Lucas Spence Strikes Again As Astros Take 4-0 Lead vs. A's

With his two-run triple, that makes it six extra-base hits and nine RBI for Lucas Spence in this four-game set. Not bad for an undrafted free agent playing in just his 19th major league game.

With a 4-0 lead and the Rangers losing 3-1, Houston is sitting pretty right now.

The Rangers Fall Behind Again, 3-1 vs. Twins

Josh Bell. Again. This time he blasts one to right for a two-run homer. He's driven in all three of Minnesota's runs.

Manny Machado Puts the Diamondbacks in a 1-0 Hole

As if the Phillies' 4-0 lead wasn't bad enough, now Arizona will have to play from behind to even have a chance to make the playoffs.

Rick Rizzs has been the radio voice of the Mariners for 41 seasons, culminating in this one. It got a little dusty at T-Mobile Park when this happened.

MacKenzie Gore Is Done After 2.1 Innings

He had only throw 25 pitches, but was about to face the Twins' batting order for the second time in the game. Definitely an aggressive move by Rangers manager Skip Schumaker.

It's his second home run off the day, and this is once again a week out from suffering multiple facial fractures. He's clearly ready for the postseason.

With his next October homer, he'll become the seventh player ever with 20 career home runs in the postseason.

Danny Jansen Goes Yard, Rangers Tie Twins 1-1

Texas has life in a must-win game. It's still 0-0 between the Astros and A's midway through the second in Sacramento.

The same isn't yet true of the actual bracket, but the schedule for the Wild Card Series is out. No surprises here at all.

Logan Gilbert fanned the side in the first against the Angels. He's the 13th pitcher this season to record 200 strikeouts, and it's the second such season of his career after 2024.

Rangers and Astros Aren't Messing Around

Either that or they're just bad, as both MacKenzie Gore and Peter Lambert ran into trouble in the first inning in Minnesota and Sacramento, respectively.

Gabriel Moreno Clinches the NL Batting Title?

Gabriel Moreno was in Arizona's initial starting lineup, but he got scratched less than an hour before first pitch.

Assuming he or Luis Arraez isn't used as a pinch-hitter today, this would seem to close the book on the race for the NL batting title. Moreno would win, .311 to .310.

Good News for Astros as Rangers Fall Behind

A sac fly in the first inning by Josh Bell made it 1-0 for the Twins over the Rangers, putting Texas on the defensive.

As a reminder, Texas needs a win and a Houston loss to make the playoffs.

Because he hit a two-run home run a week to the day from when he took a foul ball off his face while standing in the on-deck circle, causing multiple fractures.

Kyle Schwarber Doubles the Phillies' Lead vs. Rays to 4-0

Kyle Schwarber smoked this at 116.8 mph off the bat, allowing runners to score from second and third.

The Diamondbacks only just took the field in San Diego, yet their playoff hopes have already suffered a big blow.

Possibly for the last time in a major league uniform? Max Scherzer hasn't yet made that determination , but it does seem possible that the 42-year-old will call it a career.

For what it's worth, it might make his decision easier if he gets the 11 strikeouts he needs to get past Justin Verlander on the all-time leaderboard.

J.T. Realmuto Snaps Hitless Drought, Extends Phillies Lead vs. Rays to 2-0

J.T. Realmuto had been mired in an 0-for-34 slump before doubling home Edmundo Sosa. Victor Mesa Jr. didn't take a good route, but that thing was scorched at 110.5 mph.

This was after Bryce Harper had struck out looking, so good on Bryson Stott to bail him out with two down in the inning.

300 Career Home Runs for Francisco Lindor

This makes Francisco Lindor one of only three primary shortstops to top the 300-home run threshold, joining Cal Ripken Jr. (431) and Miguel Tejada (307).

For those who are wondering: Alex Rodriguez was not technically a primary shortstop, but he did hit 344 home runs as a shortstop.

Zack Wheeler Dominates the Rays in the 1st

If the Phillies are going to clinch a playoff spot today, it would help to get a vintage start from Zack Wheeler. It seems he's gotten the message, as he made quick work of three really good Rays hitters in the first.

Clinch Scenarios for AL West, NL Wild Card

Houston Astros: Win vs. Athletics or Rangers loss vs. Minnesota Twins

Texas Rangers: Win vs. Twins and Astros loss vs. Athletics

The Astros hold the tiebreaker, courtesy of a 9-4 record against the Rangers in the regular season.

Philadelphia Phillies: Win vs. Tampa Bay Rays or Diamondbacks loss vs. San Diego Padres

Arizona Diamondbacks: Win vs. Padres and Phillies loss vs. Rays

The Diamondbacks hold the tiebreaker. They and the Phillies split six games during the regular season, so the tiebreaker is determined by intra-division records. Arizona went 32-19 in the NL West, while the Phillies went 28-24 in the NL East.

articles.title: Phillies avoid disaster, clinch NL's final wild-card spot after near-collapse ahead of D-backs
articles.summary: The Phillies could have clinched a playoff spot as early as Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies can exhale. Which isn't the sign of a regular season where everything went according to plan.

With a 7-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Sunday, the Phillies clinched the third and final wild-card spot in the National League, holding off a late charge from the Arizona Diamondbacks . They will play the division rival Atlanta Braves in the wild-card round.

Philadelphia could have clinched a playoff spot as early as Wednesday, which it entered as part of a three-way tie with the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres at 87-70. The D-backs were seemingly dead in the water, four games back from the trio with five games each left to play.

As MLB reached the final day of the regular season, the Phillies entered Sunday with a one-game lead on the D-backs, but it was Arizona who held the tiebreaker. That created a clinching scenario in which the Phillies could avoid disaster with either a win or a D-backs loss.

The Phillies treated the weekend like it was facing an elimination game, first starting Aaron Nola on short rest in their 12-1 loss to the Rays on Saturday then activating Jesús Luzardo from the injured list to come out of the bullpen behind Zack Wheeler on Sunday.

Wheeler delivered what was needed with a 6-inning start consisting of 5 hits, 1 run, 0 walks and 5 strikeouts on 97 pitches. Luzardo got the ball in the eighth inning and recorded three straight groundouts before handing the ball to closer Jhoan Duran .

Meanwhile, the Phillies offense posted more runs in the first two innings than they had in the previous four games combined, with Bryson Stott , J.T. Realmuto and Kyle Schwarber all delivering RBI doubles. Disaster avoided.

Even with a loss, the Phillies would have been safe thanks to the D-backs' 9-4 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks around the same time.

The Phillies' reward will be a three-game road series against the Braves, against whom they went 4-9 this season. Advancing will be a tall order, but it beats the alternative of what would have been described as the second coming of the "Phold," the Phillies' infamous September collapse in 1964.

It will be the Phillies' fifth straight playoff berth, but they are still looking for their first World Series title since 2008. They have not won a playoff series since the 2023 NLDS.

articles.title: Mariners manager Dan Wilson won't be back for 2027
articles.summary: The Mariners have been one of the most disappointing teams in baseball this year.
articles.body:
The Seattle Mariners will have a new manager in 2027.

Dan Wilson, the team's current skipper, informed players and staff that he will not be returning to his role next season, per multiple reports. It's unclear if he will remain with the organization with a different job.

The Mariners confirmed the news hours later, with president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto saying "it was concluded" that Wilson wouldn't return following conversations over the past week.

"Collectively we failed to meet our own expectations this season," Dipoto said. "Dan and I both care deeply about this organization, these players, and the future of the Mariners. After much discussion it was concluded that a new direction is best for 2027 and beyond.

"I want to thank Dan for his efforts over the past two years and specifically recognize his role in our club advancing to Game 7 of the ALCS in 2025."

Wilson's departure as manager comes after one of the most disappointing seasons in Mariners' history , which is saying a lot for a team that has seen so much disappointment. Seattle, which came within one game of its first World Series last season, instead finished the season below .500 and out of the playoff race.

Star players like Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodríguez experienced notable slumps, while the Mariners' mediocre bullpen let key games slide throughout the season. Seattle's talented but overstuffed starting rotation also created challenges, with Wilson attempting to even things out with a "piggyback" plan that was unpopular among his pitchers.

Dipoto and general manager Justin Hollander are reportedly expected to return next season, per MLB.com . Next year would mark Dipoto's 12th season in the position, and Hollander's 11th.

Wilson, a member of the Mariners Hall of Fame who has worked for the organization as a player, broadcaster, executive and coach going back to 1994, lasted just over two seasons as manager before it fell apart. Wilson was hired by the Mariners in 2024 after the team fired longtime manager Scott Servais in the middle of another disappointing season.

At the time, Wilson's hire was a bit of an eyebrow-raiser: The former catcher had no previous managerial experience and appeared to be hired more for his ties to the franchise. He also did not start with an "interim" tag on his title, but started out as the full-fledged manager right away.

Still, something clicked last season, as the Mariners hit 90 wins, winning the American League West for the first time since 2001 and making the playoffs for just the third time this century. Seattle beat the Detroit Tigers in the ALDS to advance to the ALCS, but the M's lost to the Toronto Blue Jays after Toronto forced a Game 7, which the Jays won.

With expectations higher than ever heading into 2026, the dramatic fall-off leaves the Mariners looking for a scapegoat; Wilson, it seems, is the one who fit the bill.

articles.body:
Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Trump administration are considering hosting a baseball game in a national park, according to a new report.

The Washington Post reported Saturday that MLB and White House officials told the outlet that the league had broached the topic of a game happening at a national park to the Trump administration. Two sources close to the situation said that the administration had looked for areas in Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming for the construction of a baseball park for an MLB game.

According to a statement the Post obtained from the White House, the league questioned “if it was possible to host a game at a national park, similar to the Field of Dreams game,” referencing a game MLB occasionally hosts in Iowa , celebrating the 1989 movie.

“This is not a Presidential directive, nor is it being directed by the White House. It’s also not being driven by the Department of Interior,” the White House added. “Therefore, this is not a White House or Administration priority.”

The Hill has reached out to the White House and MLB for comment on the reported plan.

The Trump administration has a history of looking to private use of national park land, recently eyeing a land swap that would hand over a portion of Yosemite National Park to a private company, per a document submitted to Congress.

The National Park Service (NPS) stated in the document that a landowner was aiming to link their property with a park service road to facilitate commercial development.

The agency said it was “working with the landowner on a land exchange that will … enable NPS to convey an interest in land.”

WITH ONE MONTH LEFT, AMERICAN LEAGUE TEAMS ARE HEADING TOWARDS AN EMBARRASSING, HISTORIC LOW But the Astros, even with a win, did in fact make an embarrassing type of history: they are officially the worst division-winning team in baseball history. The previous low-water mark was the 2005 San Diego Padres, who won the NL West with an 82-80 record. And while the Astros won 9-0 over the long-eliminated Athletics to avoid the 80-82 record, 81–81 marks a new low winning percentage for a division winner over a full season. Inconsistent hitting with runners in scoring position. The randomness of baseball. Or a dominant closer who shuts the door consistently in close games. This year's 81-81 division winning Astros team was so bad they were outscored 32 runs over the course of the season, good for just an 78-84 expected win-loss record. While the Rangers and their fans are sure to be disappointed with the outcome, missing out on the final day, they were even worse. Texas had a -46 run differential, and a 76-86 expected record. These are not good baseball teams. So it's a near-certainty that Houston will make a quick postseason exit, right? Yeah, no, not at all. Chicago's a better team, but the randomness inherent in the small sample size of a playoff series makes the result effectively a toss up. Cleveland may be slight favorites in that series, maybe 57-43, but hardly a foregone conclusion. Which means we could be staring down the barrel of an 81-81 team reaching the ALCS. MLB always hoped for last-minute drama by starting every game around the same time on the final day of the regular season. They got it. articles.title: Max Scherzer Narrowly Misses Mark for $1M Blue Jays Contract Bonus for 2026 MLB Season
articles.summary: Toronto Blue Jays veteran starter Max Scherzer turned back the clock with seven strikeouts in Sunday's 5-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds for his 225th career victory, but it wasn't enough to secure one of his contract bonuses.
articles.body:
Toronto Blue Jays veteran starter Max Scherzer turned back the clock with seven strikeouts in Sunday's 5-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds for his 225th career victory, but it wasn't enough to secure one of his contract bonuses.

Scherzer pitched seven strong innings (on 114 pitches) on three days of rest in Sunday's win and came out to start the eighth, but he walked the first batter he faced before being removed from the game. The 42-year-old finished the season with 84.2 innings pitched, falling one out short of earning a $1 million contract incentive.

Per Spotrac , Scherzer already earned $2 million for surpassing 65 and 75 innings pitched this season. He had $1 million in incentives available for every 10 innings he pitched after 75 innings.

Of course, the Blue Jays could choose to reward Scherzer with his $1 million bonus despite barely missing the mark. The New York Yankees famously still gave Hall of Famer CC Sabathia a $500,000 performance bonus even though he was ejected from his final regular-season start six outs shy of the 155 innings needed to fulfill the incentive.

Scherzer could be nearing the end of his legendary career, so it was fun to see him in vintage form in Sunday's regular-season finale.
